modules.title: The five moments, revisited
modules.summary: When to clean hands at the bedside, with ward-specific examples.
modules.body: Before touching a patient. Before a clean or aseptic procedure. After body-fluid exposure risk. After touching a patient. After touching patient surroundings. Most missed opportunities on our wards happen at moment 5, after touching bed rails and monitors.

modules.title: Central line bundle: insertion and maintenance
modules.summary: Why Medical ICU’s CLABSI rate is rising, and the five checks that prevent it.
modules.body: Insertion: hand hygiene, maximal barrier precautions, chlorhexidine skin prep, avoid femoral site. Maintenance: scrub the hub for 15 seconds, change dressings when soiled, review line necessity daily and remove lines that are no longer needed.

modules.title: CRE: contact precautions that actually work
modules.summary: Single room or cohorting, dedicated equipment, and screening contacts.
modules.body: Place CRE patients in single rooms or cohort them. Use gown and gloves on entry. Dedicate stethoscopes and BP cuffs. Screen roommates and contacts with rectal swabs. Flag the patient record so precautions follow transfers.

modules.title: Catheter necessity: remove it today
modules.summary: A daily question that cuts CAUTI.
modules.body: Ask every day whether the urinary catheter is still indicated. Valid reasons are few: urinary retention, accurate output monitoring in the critically ill, perioperative use, and comfort at end of life.
